summary: Lake County, OR: a crow's nest dated to 1913, still there in 1993 and marked abandoned; no source describes the site since then.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says still there in 1993 and abandoned; no source describes the site after 1993

events.note: Firelookout.com dates the crow's nest to 1913
Firelookout.com says the crow's nest was still there in 1993
Forest Guard Lester E. Elder used Deadhorse Rim as a patrol lookout during July and August 1911 (Forest Lookouts)
A June 3, 1915 document, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says fire-finding instruments will be placed on Dead Horse Rim

evidence.supports: Crow's nest dated to 1913; still there in 1993; abandoned
Located in the Fremont National Forest
Patrol lookout on Deadhorse Rim used in July and August 1911
evidence.quote: 1911: This point was used as a patrol lookout by Lester E. Elder, Forest Guard, during the months of July and August.

evidence.supports: 1915 document said fire-finding instruments would be placed on Dead Horse Rim
evidence.quote: June 3, 1915: "Later on the fire finding instruments will be placed on Dead Horse Rim and Drakes Peak."

evidence.supports: Oregon list has a crowsnest named Dead Horse Lake, marked abandoned; the name differs from Firelookout.com's

corrections.why: Firelookout.com says still there in 1993 and abandoned; the Oregon list entry Dead Horse Lake says Abandoned. No source says the crow's nest was removed, so gone is not supported

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page for Deadhorse Rim, in the same national forest, describes a 1911 patrol lookout and a 1915 plan for Dead Horse Rim. That page does not say whether it is this crow's nest, so the two are not merged here.

The Oregon list's crowsnest entry is named Dead Horse Lake (42.55007, -120.78301), not Dead Horse, and no source gives coordinates for the Firelookout.com site to compare, so the two are not merged here.

notes_for_editor: The record says gone; the sources say still there in 1993 and abandoned, and none says it was removed, so a correction to unknown is proposed. Deadhorse Rim (Forest Lookouts, Fremont NF 35S-16E) may be this site or a neighbouring point; a 1915 document quoted there mentions instruments for Dead Horse Rim. Check Fremont-Winema NF records before merging. The record's kind platform fits the vocabulary entry for crow's nests. Staffing, access and visit are omitted because no source covers them. No photos found. The Lake County Museum document is cited only through the Forest Lookouts page. The Oregon list's Dead Horse Lake entry (42.55007, -120.78301) has a different name, and the Deadhorse Rim page says a trail ran from Deadhorse Lake to the rim; check the coordinates against Firelookout.com's site before merging.
